name: Forehand chop
summary: A long down-and-forward stroke from far back that returns topspin with heavy backspin.
whenToUse: As a defender against loops to your forehand, from one to three metres back.

keyPoints.stance: Side-on: left foot forward for a right-hander's forehand chop (right foot forward if left-handed).
keyPoints.bodyAction: Turn the shoulders away as the bat goes up, then turn back into the stroke.
keyPoints.strokeLength: Long: from shoulder height down to knee height.
keyPoints.timing: As the ball drops, beside the body.
keyPoints.batArm: Bat open; brush down and forward under the ball. More open = more backspin.
keyPoints.recovery: Step back to the middle with the stroke.
keyPoints.anticipation: Heavy loops kick up off the bat: keep the bat more upright and chop more down. Light loops: open the bat more and go forward.

cues: Wait for the ball to drop

learningPath.task: Watch from the side: the bat goes from shoulder to knee.
learningPath.passCheck: You can say the three cues.

learningPath.task: Follow-along far back from the table.
learningPath.passCheck: 3 sets of 10, then yes to all self-checks.
selfChecks: Did the bat start at shoulder height?
Did you finish low and forward?

learningPath.task: Chop slow topspin to your forehand.

gamePatterns.situation: A looper attacks your forehand repeatedly.
gamePatterns.how: Chop deep and low, vary heavy and light backspin, wait for the weak loop.

causes: Too much down, not enough forward
Bat too open against heavy topspin
fixes: Keep the bat more upright against heavy loops

causes: Bat too closed against a light or slow loop
fixes: Open the bat more against light topspin

penholdNotes: Penhold choppers are rare; the forehand chop works the same with an open face.
